_comment: Validate-mode golden: design §9's leakage checker, over a
hand-written roster (no Clang needed, so this runs on every lane).
`optional`'s roster carries one entry per *visible* disposition -- each
of which must stay silent wherever the wording names it -- plus the four
invisible ones the checker reports: an unmarked private member, an
`\omit`ted one, a `\merge`d twin, and one declared but never described.
The wording below names each of them in a different kind of fragment, so
the contexts differ as well as the messages: an itemdecl, an extracted
*Equivalent to:* body (§9's headline case), backticked prose, an
itemized condition, and a class-general free paragraph.
`nullopt_t` is the negative control that costs the most to get wrong. It
is a documented class whose *constructor* is `\omit`ted, so its roster
carries an invisible entry sharing the class's own name -- naming the
type in an itemdecl must stay silent. `hard_reset` appearing twice in one
body is the other control: one finding, at its first appearance.
`engaged` (an `\expos` member) and `size` (described) are named in the
same fragments as the leaks, so a run that reported them would show up
here rather than in a corpus regeneration.
`hard_reset` draws a coverage finding as well as a leakage one, and that
is the point rather than noise: `undocumented` is the one disposition
both rules report, because a declaration that is never described is both
unaccounted for (direction 1) and invisible to a reader who meets its
name in an *Equivalent to:* body.
